title: gofib: Go CLI printing the first 100 Fibonacci numbers
description:
Build a small Go CLI named gofib in this repository.

Requirements:
- Go module 'gofib' at the repository root (go.mod, go 1.27).
- Command 'gofib' prints the first 100 Fibonacci numbers, one per line, prefixed with their index, e.g. '1: 1', '2: 1', '3: 2', ... up to '100: 354224848179261915075'.
- F(100) exceeds int64: use math/big.
- Package main lives in main.go; the Fibonacci computation lives in a separate function Fib(n int) *big.Int so it is unit-testable.
- Add fib_test.go with table-driven tests covering F(1), F(2), F(10), F(100).
- No external dependencies (stdlib only).
- 'just qualitygate' must pass: gofmt clean, go vet, go build ./..., go test ./...

Done when: running 'go run .' prints exactly 100 lines with correct values and the quality gate is green.

title: gofib: add -n flag to control how many Fibonacci numbers are printed
description:
Extend the existing gofib CLI with a -n flag.

Requirements:
- Default behavior unchanged: 'gofib' prints the first 100 Fibonacci numbers, one per line, '<index>: <value>'.
- 'gofib -n 10' prints exactly the first 10 numbers in the same format.
- Use the flag package (stdlib). The flag must be named n, usage text must explain the default.
- n must be >= 1; invalid values (0, negative) cause a non-zero exit with an error message on stderr.
- Extend fib_test.go: table-driven tests for n=1, n=10, and the default path; one test for the error case (n=0) asserting non-zero exit and stderr message (use os/exec or extract the run logic for testability).
- No external dependencies. 'just qualitygate' must pass.

Done when: 'go run . -n 5' prints exactly 5 lines with correct values and the gate is green.

title: gofib: add -json flag for machine-readable output
description:
Extend the gofib CLI with a -json output mode.

Requirements:
- New bool flag 'json' via the flag package: 'gofib -json' or 'gofib -json -n 5'.
- JSON mode emits one JSON object per line (JSON Lines), each object exactly:
  {"index": <int>, "fib": "<value-as-string>"}
- fib values are big numbers; serialize them as strings to stay JSON-safe.
- Text mode (default) unchanged: '<index>: <value>'.
- Both flags combine: -json -n 10 emits exactly 10 JSON lines.
- Invalid usage (n < 1) still exits non-zero with stderr error, in both modes.
- Extend fib_test.go: table-driven tests for run() covering json+n=1,
  json default, and combined -json -n 10; assert exact JSON lines
  (unmarshal each line and compare fields).
- No external dependencies (stdlib only: encoding/json allowed).
- 'just qualitygate' must pass.

Done when: 'go run . -json -n 5' emits exactly 5 valid JSON lines with
correct fib values and the gate is green.

title: gofib: add -pretty flag for aligned column output
description:
Extend the gofib CLI with a -pretty output mode.

Requirements:
- New bool flag 'pretty' via the flag package: 'gofib -pretty', 'gofib -pretty -n 10', and 'gofib -pretty -json' are all valid.
- Pretty TEXT mode: two aligned columns, right-aligned index and value:
    '   1:                    1'
    '   2:                    1'
    '  10:                   55'
    ' 100:  354224848179261915075'
  The index column width is the width of the largest index; the value column width is the width of the largest value. Both right-aligned, separated by ': '.
- The largest index/value depend on n: for -n 5 the widths come from the 5th line, not the 100th.
- Pretty JSON mode: JSON Lines, same objects as -json ({"index":<int>,"fib":"<string>"}); -pretty only affects text mode. Document this in the flag usage text.
- -pretty with -n: both combine (pretty text for exactly n numbers).
- Default output (no -pretty) unchanged: '<index>: <value>' with single spaces.
- Extend fib_test.go: table-driven tests for run() covering pretty+n=5 (exact expected 5 lines including padding), pretty default (assert line count 100 and the exact last line), pretty+json (identical lines to -json for n=3). Compute expected strings in tests, do not hardcode F-values beyond small n.
- No external dependencies. 'just qualitygate' must pass.

Done when: 'go run . -pretty -n 5' prints the exact aligned 5-line block above (widths from the 5th line) and the gate is green.

Merged from run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0 (implementer + gate green; reviewer died on z.ai broken pipe, transient_infra — human override, output manually verified: -pretty -n 10/-n 12/default widths correct).

title: gofib: add -version flag
description:
Add a -version flag to the gofib CLI.

Requirements:
- New bool flag 'version' via the flag package: 'gofib -version'.
- With -version, print exactly one line to stdout: 'gofib <semver>' with
  semver taken from a package-level const Version = "1.3.0", then exit 0.
- -version takes precedence over all output modes: 'gofib -version -pretty'
  and 'gofib -version -json -n 5' also print only the version line.
- Add a table-driven test covering run() or main-level behavior for
  -version alone and -version combined with -json (assert the single
  version line and exit 0).
- No external dependencies. 'just qualitygate' must pass.

Done when: 'go run . -version' prints 'gofib 1.3.0' and the gate is green.

title: gofib: add README with usage and flag reference
description:
## Goal

A README.md at the repo root that documents the gofib CLI: what it is
(Go CLI printing Fibonacci numbers), install/build via mise/just,
usage, and the full flag reference.

## Flag reference to cover

- `-n <int>`: how many numbers to print (default 100, must be >= 1)
- `-json`: JSON Lines output, one object per number (`{"index":<int>,"fib":"<string>"}`)
- `-pretty`: aligned column output
- `-version`: print version and exit

Use the vocabulary from CONTEXT.md (text mode, JSON mode, count flag).
Show real example invocations and their actual output — run the built
binary to capture it, do not invent output.

## Acceptance

- README.md exists at the repo root
- Examples match actual binary behavior
- `just qualitygate` green

title: gofib: add -start flag to begin printing at a given index
description:
## Goal

A `-start <int>` flag: the first Fibonacci index to print. Default 0.
Combines with `-n` (how many), `-json`, and `-pretty`.

## Semantics

- `-start 10 -n 5` prints indices 10..14 in the active output mode
  (text mode line format stays `<index>: <value>`).
- Validation mirrors the `-n` contract: values < 0 exit non-zero with a
  stderr error message.
- `-start` must not change what `-n` counts (still the number of lines).

## Acceptance

- Flag parsed via the flag package; `Fib(n)` stays the only computation
  (no inline recomputation — see CONTEXT.md).
- Table-driven tests: default start, start+n combination, start with
  -json and -pretty, negative start rejected.
- README.md flag table gains the `-start` row; example invocation with
  REAL output captured from the built binary (do not invent output).
- `just qualitygate` green

title: gofib: add -limit flag to cap output size safely
description:
## Goal

A `-limit <int>` flag: hard cap on the LARGEST index gofib will print,
independent of `-start`/`-n`. Protects against accidental huge output
when `-n` is large (e.g. `-n 100000` should still stop at the limit).

## Semantics

- `-limit <int>`: do not print any index > limit. Default: no limit.
- Combines with `-start` and `-n`: the effective output is the
  intersection of all three (start <= index <= limit, at most -n lines).
- Validation mirrors existing flags: values < 0 exit non-zero with a
  stderr error message.
- `-limit` smaller than `-start` produces empty output (zero lines),
  NOT an error — document this in the README.
- `-json` and `-pretty` combine as usual on the reduced set.

## Acceptance

- Flag parsed via the flag package; `Fib(n)` stays the only computation
  (no inline recomputation — CONTEXT.md).
- Table-driven tests: default (no limit), limit caps large -n, limit+start
  intersection, limit < start gives empty output and exit 0, negative
  limit rejected, limit with -json and -pretty.
- README.md flag table gains the `-limit` row with a REAL example
  invocation and its actual output (capture from the built binary, do not
  invent output).
- `just qualitygate` green

title: gofib: add -seed flag for reproducible index selection
description:
## Goal

A `-seed <int>` flag: print ONLY the Fibonacci number at a given index
(one line) — a tiny lookup mode instead of a range, for spot-checks and
scripting against specific indices.

## Semantics

- `-seed i` prints exactly one entry for index `i` in the active output
  mode: text mode `i: <value>`; JSON mode one object
  `{"index":i,"fib":"<string>"}`; pretty mode single-row alignment.
- `-seed` overrides the RANGE flags: with `-seed 10 -n 5 -start 2` only
  index 10 prints (exactly one line). Document that precedence in the
  README row.
- `-version` keeps its top precedence (existing behavior, README pins
  it).
- Validation mirrors the other flags: values < 0 exit non-zero with a
  stderr error. `-seed 0` behaves like `-start 0`: treated as unset
  (sentinel), so plain `gofib` output stays unchanged.
- `Fib(n)` stays the only computation — no inline recomputation
  (CONTEXT.md).

## Acceptance

- Table-driven tests: single index via -seed; -seed overrides -n/-start
  (and -limit); -seed 0 sentinel; -seed with -json and -pretty;
  negative rejected; -version still wins.
- README.md flag table gains the `-seed` row with a REAL example
  invocation and its actual output (capture from the built binary, do
  not invent output); the precedence note lives in that row.
- `just qualitygate` green

title: gofib: add -format flag for compact table output
description:
## Goal

A `-format <mode>` flag selecting the OUTPUT STYLE globally, unifying
the text/json/pretty matrix: `text` (default), `json`, `pretty`, and a
new compact `table` mode (no leading index column, values only, one
per line).

## Semantics

- `-format text|json|pretty|table` — invalid values exit non-zero with
  a stderr error listing valid modes.
- `-json` and `-pretty` remain as SHORTCUTS: `-json` == `-format json`,
  `-pretty` == `-format pretty`. If BOTH a shortcut and `-format` are
  given and they conflict (e.g. `-pretty -format json`), exit non-zero
  with a clear error — no silent precedence.
- `table` mode: values only, one per line (aligned, right-justified to
  the widest value). Composes with `-start`/`-n`/`-limit` as usual.
- `-version` still wins over everything.

## Acceptance

- Flag via the flag package; existing behavior for `-json`/`-pretty`
  UNCHANGED (regression tests pin them).
- Table-driven tests: each mode, shortcut==format equivalence, conflict
  rejection, invalid mode rejection, table+start/n/limit combos.
- README flag table gains the `-format` row with a REAL example per
  mode (capture from the built binary; do not invent output).
- `just qualitygate` green

title: gofib: -sum flag printing the checksum of the selected range
description:
## Goal

A `-sum` flag: instead of printing one number per line, print exactly one
line containing the sum of all Fibonacci numbers in the selected range.
Natural next flag after -limit: it exercises range selection (-start,
-limit, -n) with a different aggregation and keeps the loop testing the
same surface (flag parsing, validation, format modes, README, tests).

## Semantics

- `-sum` (bool, default false): when set, gofib prints one line with the
  sum of the numbers it WOULD have printed (the same intersection of
  -start/-limit/-n that line mode uses).
- Output format follows the selected mode: text prints `sum: <value>`;
  json prints one JSON object {"index_range":[first,last],"sum":"<value>"}
  (sum as string, it can exceed int64); pretty/table print the bare value.
- `-seed` with `-sum` is an error: -seed already collapses the range to one
  index; exit non-zero with a stderr message naming both flags.
- Zero selected numbers (e.g. -limit < -start): sum prints 0, no error —
  mirrors -limit semantics.
- `-version` precedence is unchanged.
- Values stay big.Int end to end (CONTEXT.md: Fib(n) stays the only
  Fibonacci computation; the sum accumulates big.Ints, no float/string math).

## Acceptance

- Flag parsed via the flag package; validation mirrors existing flags.
- Table-driven tests: default range sum, sum with -start/-limit narrowing,
  empty range -> 0, -seed + -sum rejected, each format mode renders the sum,
  -version precedence.
- README: -sum documented in the flag reference with one example line.
- Gate green (format, vet, build, test).

title: gofib: add -format csv output mode
description:
Extend the -format family with a fifth mode csv.

Requirements:
- 'gofib -format csv' emits one CSV record per line: '<index>,<fib>' (index decimal int, fib value unquoted string; values contain no commas/quotes so no quoting rules are needed). No header line — one-record-per-line symmetry with JSON mode.
- Combines with -n, -start, -limit exactly like every other mode (e.g. 'gofib -format csv -n 5' prints 5 records; '-start 10 -limit 12' prints indices 10..12).
- -seed lookup mode in csv prints the single record '<index>,<fib>' for the requested index.
- -sum in csv mode prints exactly one record 'sum,<start>,<last>,<total>' (mirrors JSON mode's index_range+sum structure in CSV grammar).
- parseMode accepts 'csv'; the invalid-format error message names all five modes: text, json, pretty, table, csv. modeName returns 'csv'.
- There is NO -csv shortcut flag; only -format selects it. Shortcut agreement rules (-json/-pretty with explicit -format) are unchanged.
- Extend fib_test.go following the existing patterns: table-driven tests for csv default, csv+-n, csv+-start+-limit, csv+-seed, csv+-sum, and csv in TestRunFormatModes/ShortcutEquivalence/RejectsInvalidFormat where the mode lists appear.
- No external dependencies (stdlib only; encoding/csv allowed but fmt is sufficient).
- Update README.md flag reference: csv under -format with examples.

Done when 'gofib -format csv -n 3' prints '1,1', '2,1', '3,2', the invalid-format error lists csv, all new tests pass, and 'just qualitygate' is green.

title: gofib: consolidate flag parsing and validation into an options struct
description:
Refactor: behavior-preserving. run() currently takes 10 positional parameters and validates flags inline in scattered branches; main() owns flag parsing.

Requirements:
- Introduce 'type options struct' holding every flag value (n, start, limit, seed, format, json, pretty, version, sum) and 'parseOptions(args []string) (options, error)' that owns flag.Parse AND all validation currently inside run() (invalid n/start/limit/seed, seed+sum conflict, format validity, format-vs-shortcut disagreement) plus -o output path when it exists (see follow-up seed; design parseOptions so adding a field is the only change needed).
- run becomes 'run(w io.Writer, opts options) error' with no inline flag validation — parseOptions is the single rejection point; error strings stay byte-identical (existing tests pin them).
- main shrinks to: opts, err := parseOptions(os.Args[1:]); on error print to stderr and exit 1; else resolve writer, run.
- New table-driven TestParseOptionsInvalid covering EVERY rejection case with its exact error message (n=0, n=-1, start<0, limit<0, seed<0, seed+sum, bad format value, format=json + pretty=true disagreement, format=pretty + json=true disagreement) and TestParseOptionsDefaults pinning defaults (n=100, start=0, limit=0, seed=0, format="", all bools false).
- The -version ignore-invalid semantics (version short-circuits before validation) must be preserved: parseOptions returns the version flag without validating the rest; pin it with a test.
- No behavior change: all existing tests pass unmodified except call-site adaptation to the new run signature (table constructors updated, assertions untouched).
- No external dependencies. 'just qualitygate' green.

Done when run() has no flag validation, parseOptions is the only validator, the new tables cover every rejection, and the full suite is green.

title: gofib: add -o flag to write output to a file
description:
Add '-o <path>' (default empty = stdout, behavior unchanged).

Requirements:
- When -o is set, ALL output goes to the file: every format mode (text/json/pretty/table/csv), -sum output, and -version output. Uniform rule, no mode exceptions.
- File semantics: create or truncate (os.Create). On success print NOTHING to stdout, exit 0.
- Failure to open (unwritable directory, permission) exits 1 with 'gofib: cannot open <path>: <os error>' on stderr and no stdout output.
- Usage text explains the default (empty = stdout).
- Structure: keep run(w io.Writer, opts) unchanged; resolve the writer in main (or a small resolveOutput(path) (io.WriteCloser, error) helper added next to parseOptions). Tests: -o with a temp dir file produces byte-identical content to the equivalent stdout invocation (table across text, json, csv modes); -o to a non-creatable path returns the error; -version -o writes the version line into the file.
- No external dependencies. 'just qualitygate' green.
- Update README.md flag reference: -o with examples.

Done when 'gofib -o out.txt -n 3' writes 3 lines to out.txt, stdout stays empty, exit code 0, tests cover the modes and error path, and the gate is green.

title: develop: scope the evidence diff per seed, not per run base
description:
From the improve review of run 01M11P68SHFS165HP9ATK6094V (recommendation 1, highest impact).

Problem: evidence.nu diffs seed-work files against the RUN base, so the capture accumulates every closed seed's hunks: 21.8 KB -> 53.4 KB -> 58.1 KB across the three loops. Reviewers then page through closed-seed hunks in a blob ref (reviewer@2/@3 journals), burning 30-60 s and tool detours per review — the main 'Verification blocked' trigger.

Requirements:
- Anchor the evidence diff at the commit where the CURRENT seed was claimed (the per-seed checkpoint commit exists in the run branch history; the engine already creates a commit per stage visit).
- The capture header must name the diff base (seed-claim SHA) so the reviewer can attribute scope mechanically.
- Integrity header and seed-work file list stay run-scoped (they are small); only the diff scope changes.
- Keep -U3 context (fabro applied 2026-08-27).
- Expected: captures stay ~15-25 KB regardless of loop count; no blob demotion on single-seed captures.

Done when a 2-seed develop run's second evidence capture contains ONLY the second seed's diff hunks and the reviewer journal records context-only approval.

title: develop: make lesson capture enforceable in the implementer outcome contract
description:
From the improve review of run 01M11P68SHFS165HP9ATK6094V (recommendation 5).

Problem: implementer.md step 6 asks for 'ml record' when something durable surfaced, but it is not part of the required outcome JSON — implementer@1 recorded a textbook lesson in the journal, yet no .mulch/ change appears in any checkpoint diff. The lesson dies with the run journal.

Requirements:
- Add to the 'succeeded' outcome checklist in prompts/implementer.md one line: either an 'ml record' was run (name the mx-id) or an explicit 'nothing durable — skipped'.
- Mirror the journal-contract pattern (required keys, never optional silence).
- Keep it honest: skipping is a valid answer; only silence is a violation.

Done when the next develop run's implementer summaries all carry the record-or-skip line and at least one ml record lands when a real lesson exists.

title: Fix invalid reasoning_effort pin on planner node
description: In .fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro (planner node, line 29) change reasoning_effort="medium" to "low" or remove the node-level pin — glm-5.3 only allows low/high/max. Run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E died 1.5s into the planner stage with invalid_request: model 'glm-5.3' does not support reasoning_effort 'medium' (0 tokens, will_retry=false), failing the run with 0 of 4 seeds touched. Expected effect: the planner's first LLM call succeeds and this exact failure class becomes impossible.

title: Validate node-level model controls at submit time
description: Extend .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/sync-check.nu (or the engine submit path) to cross-check node attrs like reasoning_effort against the resolved provider/model capabilities before sandbox creation. In run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E the error was purely static (graph pins medium, provider allows low/high/max) but was only discovered after 33.4s of sandbox + setup. Expected effect: config-class errors fail in under 1s with the provider's exact message instead of a ~51s run costing a sandbox and a pushed branch.

title: Degrade on unsupported model control instead of dead-ending
description: Configure fallbacks in the run's model settings and/or add engine behavior to retry once with the unsupported control dropped on api_deterministic/invalid_request. Run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E had max_attempts=5 but will_retry=false and fallbacks = {}, so one parameter mismatch consumed the whole goal-gated run even though the error message contained the remedy. Expected effect: model swaps or control drift degrade a single call to defaults instead of failing the run.

title: Surface root-cause error in terminal run status
description: In the engine's conclusion mapping (or by dropping goal_gate=true on the planner node in workflow.fabro, since planner failure already has an explicit edge to refiner), make the terminal failure reason the original signature planner|…|invalid_request instead of 'goal gate unsatisfied for node planner and no retry target'. In run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E the visible status masked the actual model-control rejection, which lived only in stage detail. Expected effect: run lists show an actionable root cause in seconds.

title: Scope skill discovery to workflow skills dir

Run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E's agent.skills.discovered event pulled 36 skills (personal ones like ask-matt, scaffold-exercises) into a planner that only needs sd, adding discovery time and prompt bloat against a tight preamble_budget_kb=12. title: Skip empty checkpoint commits on failed runs

After the planner failed (0 tokens, 0 files changed), run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E still spent ~14s on two meta snapshots, two empty commits (dfb266e, d99a357) and two remote pushes — over half the workflow wall time, producing only branch pollution. title: Pre-install mise toolset in runner image

In run 01M0QJ01P9E6EKX8S6TQN91G8E mise install took 26.6s of the 28.5s setup on the purpose-built image for a run whose useful life was 1.5s. title: Restrict verification-only briefs to smoke-level commands
description: Add one sentence to prompts/planner.md verification-only guidance: "list smoke-level commands only (go build, go test, go run smokes); the gate belongs to the tester stage." In this run planner@2 and planner@3 briefs mandated just qualitygate under Required verification commands while implementer.md rule 4 forbids running the full gate, forcing implementer@3 to resolve the contradiction itself (painpoint #3 in .fabro/run-painpoints.jsonl).

title: Require English responses in implementer prompt
description: Add "Always respond in English" to .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md. In this run implementer@2 replied in German ("Verstanden — ich beende den Run…") to a German stop steer, and that reply leaked into later stages' context.

title: Stop restating the full painpoint list in every prompt
description: Change the painpoint sections in prompts/planner.md, prompts/implementer.md, and prompts/reviewer.md to emit only NEW entries appended directly to the append-only .fabro/run-painpoints.jsonl (which refiner.nu already delivers from), dropping the restate-the-full-accumulated-list instruction. In this run ~2.8KB was mirrored into three prompts per pass and the reviewer received the list truncated — accumulation lossy at exactly the node told to restate it; also frees preamble budget to compound with the budget raise.
